name: Bimetric Slip-Lock Escape: Hassan-Rosen with e^-y-Screened Kinetic Decoupling
claimed_mechanism: This candidate exploits the Hassan-Rosen bimetric framework to escape the DC-013 slip-lock theorem by introducing a second dynamical metric f_munu that carries the preferred-frame coupling. The massive graviton sector provides the off-ray lensing correction required for MOND, while the e^-y screening ensures that the preferred-frame PPN parameters vanish in the Newtonian limit. Crucially, the kinetic normalization of the propagating massive mode is held at an O(1) constant independent of the screening factor, thereby satisfying the P7 condition that separates the screened PPN response from the finite kinetic normalization. The MOND dynamics are implemented through the auxiliary Legendre field chi, which enforces the frozen mu(y)=1-e^-y kernel.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the bimetric structure yields two distinct gravitational potentials: one from g_munu and one from f_munu. The massive graviton mode mediates an additional force that modifies the Poisson equation to produce MOND scaling, while the tensor sector maintains c_T=1 due to the Hassan-Rosen potential's special form. The e^-y screening ensures that the preferred-frame coupling (which would otherwise violate PPN constraints) is suppressed by a factor of e^-y in the high-acceleration regime, recovering standard GR in the Solar System. The lensing potential is boosted relative to the Newtonian potential by a factor determined by the bimetric mixing, yielding the correct MOND lensing behavior without violating the slip-lock theorem.
inequivalence_argument: This architecture is genuinely inequivalent to all dead classes because it introduces a second dynamical metric, which is explicitly outside the scope of DC-001 (local single-metric), DC-013 (frame-free single-metric slip-lock), and DC-012 (frameless localized-nonlocal). The bimetric structure provides a legitimate off-ray escape from the slip-lock theorem because the two metrics can couple to different combinations of (Phi, Psi), breaking the diff-invariance lock that forces frame-free theories onto the delta-R ray. The e^-y screening of the preferred-frame coupling avoids the P2 kill (unscreened PF), and the independent O(1) kinetic normalization avoids the P7 strong-coupling wall that killed the khronometric candidate (DC-010). Unlike DC-002 (AeST), there is no 6-DOF aether with constant coupling; the preferred-frame effect is carried by the bimetric mixing, which is screened. Unlike DC-005 (disformal scalar), the second sector is a full metric, not a scalar disformal factor, and it provides genuine tensor-mode lensing correction.
